group_1c_trefoils_trays_covered_trench.desc: racks/trays in covered trench, restricted air circulation, trefoils spaced 2 De horizontally, tiers 300 mm apart

kei_tech_handbook.basis: Is at 90 C conductor, 30 C ground, 40 C air, 150 C.cm/W, depth 90 cm (3.3/6.6/11 kV) or 105 cm (22/33 kV); SC 250 C; Ia = K x Is; one circuit.

group_1c_trefoil_ground.key: trefoil groups -> spacing between trefoil group centres (mm)

group_3c_perforated_trays_touching.desc: vertical spacing between trays 300 mm, >=20 mm from wall

comparison_with_lv_is3961: Ground temperature: MV XLPE factors (Polycab 15/20/25/35/40/45 C = 1.12/1.08/1.03/0.96/0.91/0.87; KEI identical except 25 C = 1.04) are much flatter than data/derating_is.json 'ground_temp_pvc' (1.17/1.12/1.06/0.94/0.87/0.79), which is for 70 C PVC. Do not reuse the PVC table for MV XLPE.

Soil resistivity: Polycab MV 100/120/150/200/250/300 C.cm/W = 1.20/1.11/1.0/0.89/0.80/0.73, one factor for all sizes. The LV IS 3961 table in derating_is.json is size-dependent and milder (e.g. small sizes 100 -> 1.10, 200 -> 0.92). KEI publishes no MV soil-resistivity table.
Depth: MV reference depth is 900 mm (<=11 kV) / 1050 mm (22-33 kV); LV reference is 750 mm. Depth factors are relative to different references and not interchangeable.

Grouping: Polycab MV 1-core trefoil-in-ground factors (3.3-22 kV, 2 groups touching 0.78, 3 -> 0.68, 4 -> 0.61, 5 -> 0.56) are close to but not identical to LV IS 3961 Table 6 (0.76, 0.66, 0.61, 0.56); 33 kV has its own column. Polycab MV multicore tray (touching) and horizontal-in-ground factors are numerically identical to the LV tables already in derating_is.json. KEI uses IEC-style tables (spacing 200-800 mm between group centres) with lower touching factors (e.g. 1-core 2 trefoils touching 0.73).

Air temperature: Polycab/KEI MV XLPE air factors 25..50 C = 1.14/1.10/1.04(KEI 1.05)/1.00/0.95/0.90(KEI 0.89). The LV air_temp table in derating_is.json is currently null, so no direct comparison was possible.

xlpe_90_to_250C.confirmation: Polycab Table 2 (1 s short-circuit, XLPE, 90 C operating / 250 C final) reproduces k x S: Cu 1000 mm2 -> 142.9 kA (k = 142.9), 95 mm2 -> 13.6 kA (143 x 95 = 13.585 kA); Al 1000 mm2 -> 94.3 kA (k = 94.3), 120 mm2 -> 11.3 kA (94 x 120 = 11.28 kA).
xlpe_90_to_250C.formula: I_sc(t) [A] = k x S [mm2] / sqrt(t [s]); Polycab: It = Ish / sqrt(t)
xlpe_90_to_250C.caveat: One older-edition IEC reproduction lists Al = 93; the Polycab table implies 94.3, current IEC reproductions give 94.

k_values.screen_and_armour_note: Neither Polycab nor KEI publishes copper-screen or armour short-circuit capability. Would need IS 7098-2 screen-area requirements + IEC 60949 calculation - not sourced here.

voltage_drop_limits.jurisdiction: Nepal (NEA distribution planning, AIIB-financed Power Distribution System Upgrade & Expansion Project)
voltage_drop_limits.level: 33 kV sub-transmission lines and 11 kV MV feeders
voltage_drop_limits.basis: Voltage drop at target-year loading computed from the source grid substation (tap-off drops added); conductor size or double circuit chosen to keep drop < 5%. Standard 11 kV conductors 100 mm2 Dog, 50 mm2 Rabbit, 30 mm2 Weasel ACSR.
voltage_drop_limits.quote: the voltage drop at target loading year will be computed, and then conductor size will be selected to maintain a voltage drop less than 5%

voltage_drop_limits.jurisdiction: India - Indian Electricity Rules 1956, Rule 54 (statutory supply tolerance; carried into state Supply Codes)
voltage_drop_limits.level: High voltage (>650 V up to 33 kV), at consumer point of supply
voltage_drop_limits.basis: Permitted deviation of supply voltage from declared voltage. This is an end-of-line supply tolerance, not a per-feeder design drop budget.

notes: PRIMARY SOURCE for complete R/X/C/SC + ampacity: Polycab HT XLPE catalogue (IS 7098-2 basis). SECOND SOURCE for ampacity/C/X cross-check: KEI Technical Handbook (adds trefoil vs flat single-core ratings).

Polycab Table 1 (R) and Table 2 (1 s SC) are per conductor size, shared by all voltage grades; they were copied into every Polycab row of that size. KEI rows have R and SC = null: KEI p.156 conductor data was not transcribed in full (spot-check at 95 mm2: Cu 0.193 DC / 0.247 AC90, Al 0.320 / 0.410 ohm/km - matches Polycab).

Polycab 1-core reactance: x_ohm_km = 'Arm' column, x_ohm_km_unarmoured = 'Un-Arm' column. KEI publishes reactance for multicore cables only, so KEI 1-core x_ohm_km = null. KEI 3.3 kV 3-core capacitance taken from the 3.3 kV 'ARMOURED' column of p.97 (an 'UNARMOURED' column also exists).

Polycab Table 3 (1-core capacitance) and Table 5 (1-core reactance) have an EMPTY 35 mm2 row and values start at 50 mm2; for 12.7/22 and 19/33 kV the reactance columns have values at 50 and 70 mm2 although those cables start at 95 mm2. A one-row shift in the published table is possible - transcribed exactly as published.
Polycab Table 5, 12.7/22 kV armoured, 500 mm2 is printed '8.099' (obvious typo, probably 0.099) - stored as null.
Polycab Table 5, 19/33 kV armoured, 400 mm2 = 0.119 > 300 mm2 = 0.112 (non-monotonic, probable typo). Stored as published.
Polycab Table 3, 6.6/6.6 & 6.35/11 kV 1-core capacitance: 500 mm2 = 0.50 < 400 mm2 = 0.53 (non-monotonic). Stored as published.
Polycab Table 20 (3.3 kV 3-core Cu) 300 mm2 in air = 510 A, while the otherwise identical 6.6 kV and 11 kV tables give 570 A; 510 also breaks the size trend. Probable typo, stored as published.

Polycab 1-core 12.7/22 kV Al 95 mm2 ground = 205 A vs 200 A at 19/33 kV; otherwise 22 kV and 33 kV ratings are identical. Polycab 11/11 kV (UE) ratings equal 6.35/11 kV (E) for overlapping sizes. Polycab 3-core 3.3 kV ratings equal the 11 kV ones (except the 300 mm2 Cu air value above).

Polycab 1-core tables do not state formation; KEI gives trefoil-touching and flat-touching separately. Polycab single-core values are slightly higher than KEI trefoil (e.g. 11 kV Al 240 mm2: Polycab 340/300/470 vs KEI trefoil 326/286/450 A ground/duct/air; 33 kV Cu 240: Polycab 430/370/600 vs KEI 404/350/575).

3-core Polycab and KEI agree closely (11 kV Al 240 mm2: Polycab 315/275/395, KEI 315/278/387; 33 kV Al 240: 310/275/400 vs 312/282/393). KEI air ratings and Cu ratings run a few % lower at large sizes.

Both catalogues: max conductor 90 C, ground 30 C, air 40 C, soil 1.5 K.m/W, depth 0.9 m (<=11 kV) / 1.05 m (22/33 kV), ducts at 30 C ground (KEI: single-way buried duct). Ratings are for ONE circuit; apply group factors.
Ampacity is manufacturer-published; IS 7098-2 itself (current edition 2011, 2nd revision) contains no ampacity tables. Both catalogues cite the 1985 edition for construction.

Not transcribed although available: KEI 1-core 1.9/3.3 & 3.3/3.3 kV (p.102), 3.8/6.6 kV, 11/11 kV UE (p.106), 12.7/22 kV (p.107) and KEI 3-core 12.7/22 kV (p.114); Polycab 3.8/6.6 kV and 33/33 kV (UE) tables. Not obtained: Universal Cables, Havells (2009 catalogue URL returned HTML, not PDF), RR Kabel, Finolex, Gloster MV tables.

Voltage drop: no official NEA Distribution Planning Criteria, Nepal Grid Code or distribution bylaw text with a numeric MV voltage-drop limit was found online. The 5% figure is from NEA/AIIB project design criteria. CEA (Measures relating to Safety and Electric Supply) Regulations 2023 text could not be downloaded to check for a successor clause; IE Rules 1956 Rule 54 (HV +6/-9%) is the long-standing statutory reference mirrored by state Supply Codes (e.g. TNERC uses 6%/10% for 11/22 kV). Nepal Electricity Regulation 2050 voltage tolerance not verified.
